summary:
I did a real 6.0.0 -> 6.1.0 upgrade in the dev container, under $TMPDIR/KDX9-* (the $TMPDIR/UPG-* prefix collided with another agent, which overwrote my first marketplace).

**Setup on 6.0.0 (npm @chrisdudek/yg@6.0.0).**
- A local marketplace git repo, $TMPDIR/KDX9-mkt. `house` is tagged pack/house@0.1.0 and has a helper module, marker.mjs. `lint` is untagged and was installed from the branch, which 6.0.0 allowed.
- A TS shop app, $TMPDIR/KDX9-app:
  - 8 components, including model/.github with an enforced script rule. Relations, and tsconfig `paths` aliases.
  - Two script rules with drills. no-console has a helper patterns.mjs. api-validates has hand-written cases under `violates-x/api/`.
  - Two prose rules. The domain type has log_required plus log entries.
  - `auto_approve: full`, and an openai-compatible tier pointed at a fake local server that returns "approved" only for `Bearer sk-fake`, with the key supplied only through OPENAI_API_KEY.
  - 3 prose verdicts from the fake reviewer, plus 1 recorded through `yg verdict record` (external judge).
  - Committed lock, PASS.
- The v6.0.0 examples/ directory, committed. All PASS except `failing`, which fails by design.

**Upgrade with candidate 1f82edbb, following "Upgrading from 6.0.0" literally.**
- Step 1 (`yg init --upgrade`) works. It lists every line it adds, and it also adds a .gitattributes line that the step does not mention. For a 6.0.0 project it prints "Agent rules already up to date" (the digest sha is identical), so the step's stated reason is moot.
- Step 2 works: `yg verdict *` exits 1 with a clear what/why/next, yg-error/1 under --json.
- Step 3 works once you already know which case to move: the drill case reported MISS with no hint, and passed after the move.
- Step 4 works: the 401 warning names OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY.
- Step 6 does not work as written for the package record (see F1), and one untagged package freezes updates for every package (F2).
- Step 8 loads .github as documented.
- Step 19 surfaced the tsconfig-alias edges, and `fix:` gave the stanza.
- Step 20 cleared the rest.

**Verdicts re-opened.**
- App: 8 of 8 script verdicts went stale, plus 1 new pair for .github. 0 of 4 prose verdicts re-opened; the external-judge verdict held and was named in a note.
- Examples: 12 of 12 script verdicts, 0 of 2 prose.
- For every stale pair the CLI said "inputs changed since the verdict (a source edit, an aspect edit, or a changed reference)". None of those was true.

Both projects got back to green. The guesswork was:
- the drill move;
- the undocumented `yg pack update --reinstall`, the only command that migrates the package record;
- no way out for the untagged package.

Side probes found two more upgrade traps that the list does not cover:
- one unknown config key, even in the gitignored yg-secrets.yaml, makes the CLI drop the whole config;
- a human notes file in a prose rule's directory now re-opens paid verdicts.

surviving.title: Upgrading step 6 is false: `yg pack update` does not record tag/commit for a package already at its newest version; only the undocumented --reinstall does
surviving.where: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] Upgrading step 6 ("each package's next `yg pack update` records them"); source/cli/src/cli/pack.ts update path
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/KDX9-app, house installed by 6.0.0 as `#house@0.1.0` from a source tagged pack/house@0.1.0. `yg pack verify` reported: 'house' 0.1.0 — the copy is exactly pack/house@0.1.0 at commit dc158579794f (the record names no commit, so only the files were compared). `yg pack update house` printed "'house' is already at 0.1.0." (rc=0), and `diff yg-packages.yaml.before yg-packages.yaml` was empty. `yg pack list` still showed "(no tag recorded — read from a plain directory, or installed by an earlier release)". Only `yg pack update house --reinstall` wrote `requested: "latest"`, `tag: "pack/house@0.1.0"` and `commit: dc1585...`, which the CHANGELOG never mentions. It then printed "Rules whose content changed need judging again. Run: yg check --approve" although nothing changed.
surviving.impact: A CHANGELOG instruction that does not work as written. Every package installed by 6.0.0 keeps a record with no tag or commit until its author happens to publish a newer version, so `pack verify` can only compare files. The user is never told the command that fixes it.
surviving.suggested_fix: Make a plain `yg pack update <name>` at the same version back-fill `tag` and `commit` when the record lacks them (it is a record migration, not a reinstall), or change step 6 to say `yg pack update <name> --reinstall`. Have `pack list` / `pack verify` name that command when the record has no tag. Drop the "content changed" line when no file changed.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-real-f1 (6.0.0 install of #house@0.1.0 --as acme/rules from a source tagged pack/house@0.1.0). 6.1 `yg pack verify house`: "the copy is exactly pack/house@0.1.0 at commit b70aea070d12 (the record names no commit, so only the files were compared)". `yg pack update house`: "'house' is already at 0.1.0." rc=0, and diff of yg-packages.yaml before/after was empty. `pack list` still says "no tag recorded ... installed by an earlier release". Only `--reinstall` wrote requested/tag/commit, and it printed "Rules whose content changed need judging again. Run: yg check --approve". The cause is source/cli/src/cli/pack-update.ts:346-373: at the same version it returns action 'none', or 'record' with {...entry, requested}, which never back-fills tag or commit. The sentence in step 6 is false for any package that is already at its newest version. Downgraded because it is a description, not the instruction. The instruction ("run yg pack verify once") works, verify still compares the files, and no gate result is wrong. What is lost: moved-tag detection stays off for those packages until the author publishes a newer version.

surviving.title: One package installed untagged by 6.0.0 blocks `yg pack update` for every package, and verify's advice for it is wrong
surviving.where: yg pack update (no name), yg pack verify; CHANGELOG Upgrading step 6 / Breaking "install only published versions"
surviving.evidence: Source had pack/house@0.1.0 and @0.2.0, and no lint tag (6.0.0 installed lint from the branch). In $TMPDIR/KDX9-app2, `yg pack update` printed "error[command-error]: '$TMPDIR/KDX9-mkt' publishes no version of 'lint'. ... Nothing was installed or changed." (rc=1), and house stayed at 0.1.0. `yg pack update house` then gave "Updated 'house' 0.1.0 → 0.2.0". `yg pack verify` for lint: "could not be compared with its source: The source has no version '0.1.0' of 'lint' ... Restore an edited copy with yg pack update <name> --reinstall; ask the publisher about a tag that moved." Following that, `yg pack update lint --reinstall` fails with "The source has no version '0.1.0' of 'lint'". verify exits 1 permanently.
surviving.impact: A consumer who did nothing wrong on 6.0.0 finds that the bare update, and a CI step running `yg pack verify` as step 6 suggests, fail until a third party tags. Updates to all other packages are silently frozen, and the next: step does not say they can be updated by name. The copy is neither edited nor was a tag moved, so both hints are wrong for this case.
surviving.suggested_fix: In update-all, update every package that can be updated, report the untagged ones at the end, and exit non-zero only for those. Give verify a separate outcome for "installed from an untagged source by an earlier release" with its own next step: keep it and pin it, or `yg pack remove` and re-add once the author tags. Say in step 6 that update-all stops on such a package.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-real-f2. The source has pack/house@0.1.0 and @0.2.0 (manifest and marketplace agree) and no lint tag; 6.0.0 had installed lint from the checkout. 6.1 bare `yg pack update`: "error[command-error]: '$TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-real-mkt2' publishes no version of 'lint'. ... Nothing was installed or changed." rc=1, and house stayed at 0.1.0. `yg pack update house` then gave "Updated 'house' 0.1.0 → 0.2.0". `yg pack verify`: "'lint' 0.1.0 does not verify: could not be compared with its source: The source has no version '0.1.0' of 'lint'", then "Restore an edited copy with yg pack update <name> --reinstall; ask the publisher about a tag that moved." rc=1. `yg pack update lint --reinstall` fails with "The source has no version '0.1.0' of 'lint'". Breaking (CHANGELOG line 59) and step 6 document that an untagged package can no longer be updated. They do not document that update-all stops for every package, that verify stays at rc=1 for good, or that verify's hint names a remedy which fails.

surviving.title: An unknown top-level key, even in the gitignored yg-secrets.yaml, drops the whole config to FALLBACK_CONFIG: false unmapped and "no reviewer" errors, and next: points at the wrong fix
surviving.where: source/cli/src/core/graph-loader.ts:189-199 (`let config = FALLBACK_CONFIG;` kept on ConfigParseError); source/cli/src/io/config-parser.ts:131-147, 328-329; CHANGELOG Upgrading list (config-unknown-key appears only under Breaking)
surviving.evidence: A copy of the green app ($TMPDIR/KDX9-app3) with a single `openai_api_key: sk-fake` line in yg-secrets.yaml. 6.0.0 ignored it. 6.1.0 `yg check --no-approve` output: `error[unmapped] 6 files belong to no node` (the project has coverage.required: [], but the fallback means the whole repo is required), then `error[config-unknown-key] yg-secrets.yaml: unknown top-level key 'openai_api_key'`, then `error[unverified] 4 pairs with no reviewer configured ... yg-config.yaml has no reviewer: section` (it has one; 4 valid committed LLM verdicts are no longer counted: "9 pairs verified (script)"). The run ends `next: Add to an existing node mapping, or create a new node...` and JSON suggestedNext says the same. With `auto-approve: deterministic` committed instead, `yg init --upgrade` printed "Agent rules already up to date — nothing changed" and "This project requires every tracked file to belong to a component..." with a coverage.excluded stanza, rc=0, and no word about the key.
surviving.impact: A key that 6.0.0 accepted in silence turns one developer's checkout into a wall of false errors. It can be machine-local, since secrets are gitignored, so CI stays green and nobody else can reproduce it. The first next: sends them to map or exclude files that were never the problem. The Upgrading list never tells anyone to look for this.
surviving.suggested_fix: When the only config error is unknown keys, keep the parsed config and report the key; do not fall back. Rank config errors as "graph did not load" so next: names the key. Make `init --upgrade` report config-unknown-key and skip its coverage advice when the config did not parse. Add an Upgrading step: "run yg check; config-unknown-key names keys 6.0.0 ignored, in yg-config.yaml or your local yg-secrets.yaml".
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-real-f3: coverage.required: [], an openai-compatible reviewer configured, one prose rule. The clean 6.1 run gives 1 error (unverified, no verdict yet). With only `openai_api_key: sk-fake` in the gitignored yg-secrets.yaml (git status clean), 6.0.0 ignores the key. 6.1 `yg check --no-approve` gives `error[unmapped] 5 files belong to no node` (false: the fallback config requires the whole repo), then `error[config-unknown-key] yg-secrets.yaml: unknown top-level key 'openai_api_key'` (its why wrongly says "yg-config.yaml accepts only"), then `error[unverified] 1 pair with no reviewer configured ... yg-config.yaml has no reviewer: section` (false). next: and JSON suggestedNext are both "Add each file to a node's mapping ... (unmapped — 3 errors need a code or graph fix)". The fallback comes from graph-loader.ts:189 (`let config = FALLBACK_CONFIG`), which is kept on ConfigParseError. The new error is listed under Breaking (line 68) but not in Upgrading. The cascade of false errors and the misdirected next: are not documented anywhere. I did not re-run the init --upgrade sub-claim.

surviving.title: Any file in a prose rule's directory (e.g. NOTES.md) is now a verdict input although it never reaches the prompt: the upgrade re-opens paid pairs, and every later notes edit re-bills
surviving.where: Rule-hash change (Breaking: "Every file in a rule's directory besides its rule files is now part of that rule's verdict"); CHANGELOG step 20 ("LLM verdicts are not affected") and step 6
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/KDX9-app4: on 6.0.0, added `.yggdrasil/aspects/requires-audit/NOTES.md` ("Examples of accepted audit calls, for humans."), approved, committed. 6.1.0 `yg check --no-approve --json` listed `requires-audit billing stale`, `requires-audit orders stale`, `requires-audit payments stale`, with fix `yg check --approve  (7 script pairs · free + 3 reviewer pairs · paid)`. `yg aspect-test --aspect requires-audit --node orders --dry-run | grep -c NOTES` gave 0, so the file is not in the prompt. After re-approving (3 reviewer calls), appending "typo fix" to NOTES.md gave `error[unverified] 3 pairs whose inputs changed since the verdict` with fix `(3 reviewer pairs · paid)`.
surviving.impact: A regression versus 6.0.0 that costs money. The upgrade re-reviews prose rules that keep documentation beside content.md, which contradicts step 20. From then on, editing a note the reviewer never sees re-bills every pair of that rule. The CLI blames "a source edit, an aspect edit, or a changed reference". This overshoots the earlier package-system M1 fix, which was about modules imported by check.mjs.
surviving.suggested_fix: For content.md rules, hash only what enters the prompt (content.md, references, companions). For script rules, hash only the module graph check.mjs/companion.mjs actually import, plus files they read. Or exclude *.md other than content.md. Fix step 20's claim, and have step 6 name prose rules with extra files as paid re-opens, with `yg check --approve --dry-run` first.
surviving.verifier: The mechanism reproduces. $TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-real-f4-notes has a prose rule with NOTES.md beside content.md and an LLM verdict recorded on 6.0.0 (verdict record). 6.1 shows `error[unverified] 1 pair whose inputs changed since the verdict  at: clear @ a`, with the generic why "a source edit, an aspect edit, or a changed reference". The control without NOTES.md ($TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-real-f4-plain) stays `PASS ... 1 pair verified (reviewer)`. `yg aspect-test --dry-run | grep -c NOTES` returns 0, so the file never reaches the prompt. But this is explicitly documented and deliberate. Breaking line 63: "Every file in a rule's directory besides its rule files is now part of that rule's verdict ... A rule directory holding such a file gets a new rule hash once and its pairs go back to unverified". Step 6 repeats it. Step 20's "LLM verdicts are not affected" refers to the grammar re-judge, so the two do not contradict. Human notes have excluded homes: log.md and dot-prefixed files. What remains is a design cost: content.md rules are over-hashed, and later edits to the notes re-bill. Not an undocumented regression.

surviving.title: Every script verdict re-opens on upgrade, and the CLI gives a false cause; steps 8/9 show red before step 20 explains it
surviving.where: yg check unverified block (cause "stale"); CHANGELOG Upgrading steps 8, 9, 20 order
surviving.evidence: App: 6.1.0 `yg check --no-approve` before any step gave `error[unverified] 7 pairs whose inputs changed since the verdict` plus `warning[unverified] 1 pair ...` (all 8 script verdicts, including api-validates, which has no helper file). why: "A verdict was recorded, but its inputs changed since (a source edit, an aspect edit, or a changed reference)". Examples: checkout-flow 3/3, no-secrets-in-logs 2/2, pure-transforms 1/1, type-level 6/6 went stale, all turning `yg check: FAIL` at step 9. Only step 20's `--approve --only-deterministic` returned them to PASS. Prose verdicts held: 4/4 app, 2/2 examples.
surviving.impact: Upgraders see red with a false explanation at step 8/9 and may hunt for an edit that never happened. The fix is free and printed, so the cost is confusion rather than money.
surviving.suggested_fix: When a script verdict lacks the new grammar/runtime record, give it its own cause ("recorded by an earlier release; re-run free"), or re-judge it silently on read. Move step 20 before the "run yg check" steps.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-real-f5 with a regex-only check.mjs that parses no syntax tree, verified on 6.0.0 (`PASS ... 2 verified (1 deterministic, 1 LLM)`). 6.1 `yg check --no-approve`: `FAIL`, then `error[unverified] 1 pair whose inputs changed since the verdict  at: no-todo @ a`, why "a source edit, an aspect edit, or a changed reference" (false; nothing changed), fix "(1 script pair · free)". `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` clears it. Step 20 documents the free re-judge but comes after steps 8/9/14-19, which say "run yg check". Its rationale ("grammar ... of every syntax tree its check read") does not match this case either, because the check reads no tree. The cost is confusion only.

surviving.title: Under auto_approve: full, the Upgrading steps' "run yg check" is a paid approval run
surviving.where: CHANGELOG Upgrading steps 8, 9, 14-19 ("Run yg check"); step 10 mentions auto_approve only for fork CI
surviving.evidence: App with `auto_approve: full`: step 8's `yg check` printed "note: auto-approve: full — bare 'yg check' will call the reviewer.", then `fill  9 pairs · 9 script (free) · 0 reviewer calls`, before the user could "settle what it reports". In the NOTES.md variant (F4), the same bare call would buy the 3 re-opened reviewer pairs straight away. Earlier, with only OPENAI_API_KEY set, the bare check made a reviewer call that got a 401, and the report said "Fix the cause named above" while the cause had only gone to stderr.
surviving.impact: The steps read as diagnostics but spend money in repositories with auto_approve: full. The failure report also points at text that is not in the report.
surviving.suggested_fix: Write the diagnostic steps as `yg check --no-approve` (or say "`--no-approve` if auto_approve is set"). Include the provider error in the unverified block's why instead of "named above".
surviving.verifier: Narrowed. The auto_approve part is deliberate opt-in and matches 6.0.0: 6.0.0 bare `yg check` with auto_approve: full also prints "auto-approve: full — bare 'yg check' will call the reviewer." and fills. 6.1 prints the same note plus how to stay read-only, so it is not a defect or a regression. The real remaining defect: with an unreachable endpoint, `yg check 2>/dev/null` shows `fix:  Fix the cause named above` on stdout, while the cause ("could not reach http://127.0.0.1:9: bad port") only went to stderr. So the report points at text that is not in it.

refuted.reason: Step 1: 6.1 `yg init --upgrade` on a 6.0.0 project printed "Agent rules already up to date." and listed every line it added, including "Added to .gitattributes: /.yggdrasil/**/log.md text eol=lf". That matches step 1's "it now lists every line it adds". The "refreshes the agent rules" wording is loose but harmless. In 6.1 the next: line reads "Delete .../check.mjs", but the same line goes on: "to add a rule of your own, put it in .yggdrasil/aspects/ outside packages/". So it does not contradict aspect-packages-dir-reserved's move advice. `--version` printing 6.0.0 on the candidate is the normal pre-release state, since package.json has not been bumped yet. Nothing here misleads enough to count.

summary:
I read the whole CHANGELOG [Unreleased] section (lines 8-279) and the 70 non-merge commits in v6.0.0..1f82edbb. I built the candidate in $TMPDIR/UPG-src and installed the real 6.0.0 in $TMPDIR/UPG-v600. I then ran scratch projects through 6.0.0 → 6.1.0: a script rule with a helper, a script rule that reads syntax trees, two prose rules (one with a NOTES.md beside it) whose verdicts were recorded through 6.0.0's `yg verdict`, a package installed by 6.0.0 from a local marketplace, `auto_approve: full` under CI, and a trailing `yg-suppress` marker. I also checked what Horde, Grain and Jarl depend on.

Upgrading steps 2 (`yg verdict` exits 1), 4 (docs), 5, 9, 12 (a plain prose verdict survives) and 20 (every script verdict re-opens and the free fill restores it) behave as written. The sharpest problems:
1. The release breaks things but is numbered as a minor version, and the documented CI recipe runs `npx @chrisdudek/yg` with no version pin.
2. The meaning of `suggestedNext` changed while the document keeps the name `yg-check/1`, which breaks the family's own contract rule.
3. Horde 6.0.0 silently finds no pending prose pairs when it runs against Yggdrasil 6.1.
4. Four changes that turn a passing gate red, or reopen paid verdicts, appear only under Fixed or are hidden inside an unrelated step.
5. The one-line `next:` calls a paid command free.
6. Two Upgrading steps are false (step 6) or leave the gate red for good (step 10).
7. About a dozen stale entries from mid-release contradict the Breaking section and the code.

surviving.title: The changes break adopters but ship as a minor release, and the documented CI recipe has no version pin, so every adopter's CI moves to 6.1.0 on publish day
surviving.where: CHANGELOG.md:6 ("adheres to Semantic Versioning"), README.md:34,171-172, docs/getting-started.md:16,362-364, source/cli/src/core/graph-loader.ts:27
surviving.evidence: Breaking (CHANGELOG 36-70) removes a command (`yg verdict package|record|read`), changes every text layout, stops `openai-compatible` reading OPENAI_API_KEY, adds new blocking errors (config-unknown-key, config-committed-api-key, aspect-source-symlink) and refuses untagged package sources. By SemVer that is a major release. The docs install with `npm install -g @chrisdudek/yg` and run CI as `- run: npx @chrisdudek/yg check --no-approve` (README.md:172), which fetches whatever version is newest. `CLI_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA = '6.0.0'` is unchanged, so neither CLI refuses a repository the other one wrote. I measured mixed-version churn in $TMPDIR/UPG-p1: after `yg init --upgrade` and a 6.1 `--approve --only-deterministic`, 6.1 prints `yg check: PASS  1 warning ... 1 pair verified (script)`, while 6.0.0 on the same commit prints `yg check: FAIL ... unverified (not yet reviewed)  1 pairs  1 nodes`. In $TMPDIR/UPG-p3, a prose-rule verdict recorded by 6.0.0 for a rule directory holding NOTES.md shows in 6.1 as `error[unverified] 2 pairs whose inputs changed since the verdict  at: astdet @ app / extra @ app`, while the rule without NOTES.md stays verified. So the two versions hash that pair differently, and each approval invalidates the other's.
surviving.impact: On publish day, CI jobs that follow the documented recipe move to 6.1.0 before anyone reads the 21 Upgrading steps. They go red on: newly detected relations in 10 languages, the trailing-suppress change, `auto_approve: full` under CI, and prose rules whose directory holds extra files (CI has no key to re-approve those). If developers stay on 6.0.0 while CI floats, paid prose pairs get re-reviewed back and forth, and each run overwrites the other's verdicts in the committed lock. Package ranges `^6.0.0`, which `yg pack new` now scaffolds, also accept a release that changes rule hashing and drill paths.
surviving.suggested_fix: Either release this as 7.0.0 (the family moves together anyway), or remove the breaking items from 6.1.0. Independently: pin the version in the CI recipe (`npx @chrisdudek/yg@<version>`), and add an Upgrading step 0: upgrade CI and every developer together, and never run 6.0.0 and 6.1.x on one repository. If the version stays 6.1.0, the family-contracts page and the CHANGELOG header must record why SemVer does not apply.
surviving.verifier: Confirmed facts: CHANGELOG.md:6 claims SemVer while [Unreleased] has a Breaking section with removals (yg verdict, OPENAI_API_KEY fallback, new blocking errors). README.md:171-172 and getting-started.md:362-364 use an unpinned `npx @chrisdudek/yg`. graph-loader.ts:27 still has CLI_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA='6.0.0'. I found no recorded rationale for the version number in Yggdrasil docs or in the rulings of the 6.1.0 loop. I reproduced the mixed-version hash split in $TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-docs-p3: 6.0.0 recorded verdicts for `plain` and `extra`, then reported `yg check: PASS ... 3 verified (1 deterministic, 2 LLM)`. On the same commit 6.1 reports `error[unverified] 2 pairs whose inputs changed since the verdict  at: astdet @ app / extra @ app` and `plain` stays verified. Overstated parts: the unpinned npx recipe was already in 6.0.0, so this release did not introduce it. The deterministic cache is local and gitignored: in $TMPDIR/verify-upgrade-docs-p1 a 6.0.0 `yg check` after a 6.1 fill left 6.1 PASS, so script pairs do not ping-pong through the committed lock, and only prose rules with extra files do. It is not a blocker because an Upgrading path exists; it is a versioning-policy and release-communication problem.

surviving.title: `suggestedNext` in `yg-check/1` changed meaning without a new schema number, breaking the family's own contract rule
surviving.where: CHANGELOG.md:39 (Breaking, Next); docs/family-contracts.md:66-70; yg-check/1 output
surviving.evidence: docs/family-contracts.md:66: "a change in what an existing field means counts as a shape change, even when the field's type is untouched". Line 70: "the next silent meaning change takes a number". Measured on the same refused pair in $TMPDIR/UPG-p1: 6.0.0 gives `suggestedNext: "Fix the listed violations, then: yg check --approve"` and 6.1 gives `suggestedNext: "edit src/app/a.js:1"`. On a pending pair, 6.1 gives `"yg check --approve  (unverified — 1 script pair · free)"`, where 6.0.0 gave `"yg check --approve"`. The schema is still `yg-check/1`, and family-contracts.md records no exception for this change.
surviving.impact: A consumer that runs or displays `suggestedNext` (an agent wrapper, a CI bot) now gets a pseudo-command (`edit <file>:<line>`) or a command with an annotation appended to it, under a schema id that promises the old meaning. Horde's `failStaleCli` guard never fires, because the schema name is unchanged.

summary:
I re-ran the first-hour adopter walk on candidate 1f82edbb. The CLI was built in $TMPDIR/adopt2-src inside the dev container. - The CI recipe in a fresh clone with CI=true, including committed auto_approve `full` and `deterministic`.
- The fork-PR advice.
- The new errors: committed api_key and symlinks (file-level and directory-level).

surviving.title: A committed api_key or a symlinked rule makes `yg context` refuse, so the agent's required pre-edit step fails

The refusal prints the exact fix (move the key to yg-secrets.yaml or an env var), and that edit clears the gate at once; revoking the key is advice and does not block. summary: I built candidate 1f82edbb in the dev container at $TMPDIR/comm2-src and drove it over scratch projects. $TMPDIR/comm2-a is a fresh keyless init. $TMPDIR/comm2-b/c/d is a 33-node project with a log_required service type, a script rule no-todo and a judgment rule readable-names; c and d are copies of b. Over those projects I walked the daily loop through these states: clean PASS, warnings only, unmapped, the log gate on a first verdict, ABORTED, refusals from the script rule, a broken relation, broken yg-node.yaml, yg-config.yaml and yg-architecture.yaml, pending judgment pairs with no reviewer, an unreachable reviewer, stale pairs and a draft rule. In each state I ran text, --json, --summary (both forms), --top, --aspect, --details, --approve --dry-run (text and --json) and --approve --only-deterministic, in a TTY and through a pipe. I also ran yg prime, yg advise, the yg log add and usage error paths, yg --help and every per-command --help, and compared against npx @chrisdudek/yg@6.0.0 where it mattered. Most of the grammar is delivered and it is good. Verdict lines, error[label] blocks with at/why/fix, the 12-row cap in every sink, --summary rollups, the ABORTED document, error[code]: on stderr with yg-error/1 on stdout, and the grouped --help all match the spec. The refusal path and the ABORTED gate path are close to spec mock-ups A and C. The weak point is the next: contract. It is built by regex-parsing the engine's prose fix strings (check-render-views.ts leadingCommand/embeddedCommand/namedFile), which breaks spec principle 6. That parsing produces an unrunnable command, removes the user-consent warning, points at the wrong file, and counts reviewer-pending pairs as code fixes. A run can also print up to three conflicting next: lines once stderr and stdout are read together. JSON parity has gaps: notes are missing from yg-check/1, next.command is a string in yg-error/1 but an array in yg-check/1, and the dry-run document's exit code differs from the process exit. summary:
I tested the family against the 6.1.0 candidate (Yggdrasil 1f82edbb, built on the host under scratchpad/final-family/cand) and against 6.0.0 (built from v6.0.0 under scratchpad/final-family/v600).

**Suites: all green.**
- Horde release/6.1.0 with HORDE_TEST_YG pointing at the candidate: 1411 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (horde-cand.log).
- Grain `npm test`: 2873 pass, 0 fail, 22 skipped.
- Grain `tests/seams.test.mjs`, with YG_BIN set to the candidate and YGG_DIR and HORDE_DIR set to the host checkouts: 7 of 7 pass. Its register line reads "33 row(s); 17 id(s) across 20 Horde script(s), 10 written by Grain — all present".

**Register: agrees both ways.**
- I grepped the ids myself with /usr/bin/grep. The session's `grep` is a shell function that dropped matches, and at first it made `yg-suppressions/1` look unread. It is read, at land.mjs:1281.
- Horde reads 17 schema ids, Grain writes 10, and every one has a row on the register.
- Grain writes `.family-candidates.grain.json` with v:1, producer grain and gate no-certified-convention, which matches the register.
- The seam copies the proposal by hand instead of running `yg adopt`. So I checked `yg adopt` itself: it copies the whole proposal `.yggdrasil/` recursively (adopt-transaction.ts:302), so the candidates file is installed with the graph.

Removing any one of the four made the candidate report `relation-undeclared-dependency` for that node.
- `grain advise --json` produces a `grain-advice/1` document that `yg advise import` accepts.

**Jarl** mentions yg only in its family blurb (README.md:143-150, CLAUDE.md:7). It calls no yg command, so there is nothing to break.

**Where it breaks:** the promises package's upgrade path, a false claim in the CHANGELOG's upgrade list, and a seam guard that no longer checks anything.

**Not findings:** `yg --version` of the candidate still prints 6.0.0 because package.json has not been bumped yet. Grain's SCHEMA_VERSION '6.0.0' matches CLI_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA '6.0.0'.

If possible, also tag `pack/promises@0.1.0` at 6a93649 (Horde v6.0.0), so the copies 6.0.0 installed verify and update cleanly to 0.2.0. surviving.title: CHANGELOG upgrade step 6 says a package's next `yg pack update` records its tag and commit; it does not
surviving.where: Yggdrasil CHANGELOG.md, [Unreleased] 'Upgrading from 6.0.0' item 6; source/cli/src/cli/pack-update.ts:373 (the 'none' action)
surviving.evidence:
CHANGELOG item 6 says: "A package record written by 6.0.0 is read as it is — every package following its newest version, with no tag or commit recorded — and each package's next `yg pack update` records them."
I tested the case where the content is the same. Installed with 6.0.0 from a source that already held the tagged content, then with the candidate:
- `yg pack update` prints "'promises' is already at 0.1.0."
- `/usr/bin/grep -E "requested|tag:|commit:" .yggdrasil/yg-packages.yaml` finds nothing.
- `yg pack list` still says "(no tag recorded — read from a plain directory, or installed by an earlier release)".
- `yg pack verify` says "(the record names no commit, so only the files were compared)".
In pack-update.ts, the no-op path returns `{ action: 'none', notes: ["'…' is already at …"] }` and writes no record. The `--to` path (:364) records only `requested`.
surviving.impact: Following the documented upgrade leaves every 6.0.0-era package record without tag or commit until the publisher ships a newer version. So `yg pack verify` can never check that the tag has not moved for those packages, and the CHANGELOG promises something that does not happen.
surviving.suggested_fix: When the installed copy is byte-identical to the resolved tag, have the no-op update write the tag and commit into the record (and `requested: latest`). Or reword item 6 to name the command that actually records them.
surviving.verifier: The factual claim reproduces. In $TMPDIR/verify-family-f1/proj2, 6.0.0 installed from a source whose content equals pack/promises@0.1.0. After that, the candidate's `yg pack update` and `yg pack update promises` both print "'promises' is already at 0.1.0." and exit 0. `grep -nE "requested|tag:|commit:"` on yg-packages.yaml finds nothing, and `pack list` still says "no tag recorded". So the CHANGELOG sentence "each package's next `yg pack update` records them" is false for the no-op case. The impact is overstated, though. `yg pack verify` still compares every file against the current tag ("the copy is exactly pack/promises@0.1.0 at commit 7afdc1230673 (the record names no commit, so only the files were compared)"), so any content drift is still caught. A tag moved to identical content is harmless. And `yg pack update promises --reinstall` does record `requested: "latest"`, the tag and the commit, and exits 0. What remains is inaccurate CHANGELOG wording with a working if unnamed command, not costly confusion.

surviving.title: The Grain seam's load-failure guard checks nothing under 6.1.0's text grammar, so a refused proposal passes
surviving.where: Grain plugins/grain/tests/seams.test.mjs:136-147 (the regex `/^ {2}([a-z][a-z-]+)/gm` over `yg check` text)
surviving.evidence:
The seam run against the candidate logs "[seams] yg check: 77 nodes loaded, codes seen: at, why, fix". In 6.1.0 the finding codes moved to column 0 as `error[<code>]`, and the indented lines are now `at:`, `why:` and `fix:`.
I reproduced it with a scratch graph containing an aspect that has no reviewer, and applied the seam's own two regexes:
- 6.0.0: `codes: aspect-reviewer-missing,rules-digest-stale,uncovered fatal: [ 'aspect-reviewer-missing' ]`.
- Candidate: `header: yg check: FAIL  1 error · 2 warnings   11 nodes`, `codes: why,fix,at fatal: []`, even though the output contains `error[aspect-reviewer-missing] aspect 'bad' has no reviewer: block ...`.
The header regex still matches, so the test passes.
surviving.impact: This is the family's only cross-repo CI gate. On 6.1.0 it reports green when Yggdrasil refuses a Grain-rendered aspect or node, with codes such as aspect-invalid, description-missing or node-invalid. That makes it a wrong gate result on the release branch itself. The CHANGELOG (Upgrading item 21) tells every script to stop reading the text, and the family's own seam did not.
surviving.suggested_fix: Run `yg check --json` in seam 1a and assert against `issues[].code` (plus `project.nodes` for the count), instead of scraping the text.
surviving.verifier: Grain release/6.1.0 plugins/grain/tests/seams.test.mjs:142-144 scrapes the codes with `/^ {2}([a-z][a-z-]+)/gm` and filters them through LOAD_FAILURES (line 65, which includes aspect-reviewer-missing, aspect-invalid and node-invalid).
